prompt_payload.task: Design a diverse library of executable semantic optimization skills for finite-pool scientific search. Each skill defines interpretable rule features plus a conservative Bayesian linear surrogate blended with strong target-only GP-UCB and GP-EI anchors.

target.title: MoleculeNet FreeSolv hydration free-energy replay
target.boundary: Field values and counts are public; target outcomes are not included.

source_transfer_evidence.boundary: Only source identity, objective, and public source-target field alignment are provided. Source outcomes, effects, support counts, and value priors are withheld.

executor.semantic_model: Rules become binary features. Revealed target outcomes fit a ridge Bayesian linear surrogate whose coefficient prior follows rule weights.
executor.anchor: A rank blend of target-only GP-UCB and GP-EI.
executor.fusion: semantic_mass_start/end controls the rank mass assigned to the semantic surrogate; the remaining mass stays on the target-only anchor.
executor.selection: Independent calibration seeds select one frozen skill. Independent held-out seeds are evaluated only after selection.

design_requirements: Use only exact field/value pairs in public_semantic_fields.

Each conditions object must map a real catalog field name directly to one exact catalog value, for example {"dominant_family": "oxide"}. Never use literal placeholder keys such as exact_field, field_name, field, or value.
Give every skill a distinct, descriptive scientific skill_id. Never copy schema placeholders such as short_unique_name or add numeric suffixes to a placeholder.
Give every skill 3-10 rules; use two-condition interactions only when scientifically meaningful.
Include at least one conservative low-semantic-mass skill.
Include at least one skill grounded only in the supplied source-target field alignment; do not imply that source outcome effects were observed.
Include at least one domain-knowledge skill.
Include a counter-hypothesis skill that reverses or downweights an uncertain source relation.
Prefer mechanistic, chemically or physically interpretable rules over arbitrary coverage rules.
Use positive weights for conditions expected to improve the target objective and negative weights for risks.
Do not claim access to target outcomes and do not output candidate identifiers.

rules.rationale: short scientific rationale

skills.hypothesis: what this skill transfers and when it may fail

cards.title: FreeSolv to Lipophilicity transferable skill
cards.summary: A molecular-property transferable skill instance using shared SMILES-derived descriptor fields as the representation bridge.
cards.content: Representation mapping: shared descriptor bins such as smiles_length_bin, hetero_atom_bin, halogen_bin, aromatic_bin, ring_token_bin, branch_bin, and double_bond_bin transfer directly because the source and target adapters use the same public vocabulary. Mechanism hypothesis: coarse SMILES-derived structure descriptors can indicate reusable molecular-property search geometry across hydration free energy and lipophilicity tasks. Model binding: transfer-card role confidence reweights the categorical GP kernel. Acquisition binding: GP-UCB remains the selector. Gate/risk boundary: value-level transfer is only allowed for shared descriptor vocabularies; dataset-local labels should not be transferred this way. Current 50-seed result: GP-UCB final_best 88.4775 / AUC 86.4578; transfer_weighted_gp_ucb_scale_1p5 final_best 88.5650 / AUC 86.6808.

cards.title: Reusable semantic feature pattern: high_aromatic_content
cards.summary: For real_moleculenet_lipophilicity, use the LLM to define the high_aromatic_content feature partition, then fit its direction and magnitude from revealed target observations.
cards.content: Evidence mode: target_only. Execution: disabled. Reusable lesson: preserve the LLM-proposed feature partition, but calibrate or remove unsupported coefficient signs before held-out evaluation.

care_knowledge_context.instruction: Use these public, previously archived cards only as reusable design lessons. Do not copy reported target values into a rule and do not imply that the current target outcomes were observed. Prefer lessons that survived held-out calibration.

rules.rationale: Halogenated non-aromatic/aliphatic regions may enhance hydration affinity via halogen-bonding with water, while avoiding aromatic stacking that reduces solvent accessibility.
Low heteroatom count may reduce polarity and hydrogen-bonding capacity, potentially decreasing favorable aqueous interactions.
Moderate branching can increase molecular surface area and create cavities favorable for water binding without excessive hydrophobicity.
Shorter SMILES often correspond to smaller, more polar molecules with higher solubility and hydration affinity.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the structural hypothesis that halogenation in non-aromatic contexts promotes hydration. May fail if halogen bonding is weak or if aromatic rings are needed for specific binding motifs.

rules.rationale: High heteroatom count increases polarity and hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor capacity, strongly favoring hydration free energy.
Absence of ring structures may increase conformational flexibility and solvent-accessible surface area for water interaction.
Lack of double bonds may reduce molecular rigidity and polarity, potentially decreasing specific aqueous interactions.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the general principle that polar surface area enhances hydration. May fail if excessive polarity leads to poor membrane permeability or if specific rigid scaffolds are required.

rules.rationale: Conservative weight based solely on source-target field alignment for aromatic_bin, without assuming effect direction from source outcomes.
Minimal weight reflecting field mapping from source, agnostic to target effect.
Neutral weight based on schema alignment, awaiting target calibration.

skills.hypothesis: Grounds skill only in supplied source-target field alignment, avoiding transfer of unobserved source effects. May fail if alignment is non-informative, but protects against negative transfer.

rules.rationale: Non-aromatic, linear molecules may form a hydrophobic core with a polar shell, optimizing entropy of hydration.
Moderate heteroatom count balances hydrophilicity and lipophilicity for optimal hydration free energy.
Low ring count may allow sufficient flexibility for water organization without excessive hydrophobicity.
Few double bonds maintain moderate polarity and prevent over-rigidity.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers a domain-knowledge model of amphiphilic balance for hydration. May fail if specific aromatic or rigid structures are critical for high affinity.

rules.rationale: Reverses uncertain source relation; high aromaticity without halogens may promote pi-stacking with water or polar aromatics, enhancing hydration.
Downweights absence of heteroatoms as a strong negative, countering potential over-reliance on heteroatom counts from source.
High branching may create steric hindrance reducing solvent accessibility, a counter to assumptions of beneficial complexity.

skills.hypothesis: Counters uncertain source-derived relations by emphasizing aromaticity without halogens and downplaying heteroatom absence. May fail if halogen bonding is indeed critical or if heteroatoms are essential.

rules.rationale: Very long SMILES may indicate large, hydrophobic molecules with poor hydration affinity.
High ring count often correlates with rigidity and hydrophobicity, potentially unfavorable.

skills.hypothesis: Uses minimal semantic guidance to avoid overcommitment, heavily relying on target-only GP-UCB for exploration. May fail if strong semantic signals exist but are ignored.

rules.rationale: Unbranched chains may have lower conformational entropy change upon hydration, reducing favorable entropy contribution.
Moderate double bond count introduces rigidity and polarity, optimizing enthalpy-entropy balance for water binding.
Moderate aromaticity can provide polarizable pi-systems for water interaction without excessive hydrophobicity.
Low halogenation may offer mild polarity enhancement without steric or toxicity issues.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers an entropy-focused model of hydration, emphasizing molecular flexibility and moderate polarity. May fail if enthalpy-dominated interactions are primary.

rules.rationale: Mid-sized molecules with low heteroatom count may have optimal size-to-polarity ratio for hydration free energy.
Complete lack of rings and double bonds may indicate saturated alkanes with high hydrophobicity and poor hydration affinity.
Moderate halogenation in non-aromatic systems may enhance polarity and halogen-bonding without aromatic quenching.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers a composite descriptor approach using interactions of size and polarity features. May fail if interactions are non-additive or if key features are omitted.
